flawed_step: The universal assertion fails for the Petersen graph.
counterexample: Let indices be modulo 5. Take vertices a_0,...,a_4,b_0,...,b_4 and edges a_i a_{i+1}, a_i b_i, and b_i b_{i+2}. This finite simple graph is 3-regular. It is 3-connected: identify it with the graph whose vertices are the 2-subsets of {1,2,3,4,5}, adjacent when disjoint. Any deleted pair is, up to a permutation, either {12,34} or {12,13}. After those deletions, respectively, the remaining vertices have spanning paths 25-14-35-24-15-23-45-13 and 45-23-14-25-34-15-24-35, so deletion of any two vertices leaves the graph connected. It has no Hamiltonian cycle. Such a cycle would use an even number of the five spokes a_i b_i, hence 2 or 4. With 2 spokes i,j, its restrictions to the outer and inner 5-cycles would be spanning paths. The outer path requires j-i=±1 mod 5, while the inner path requires j-i=±2 mod 5, impossible. With 4 spokes, rotate so that a_0b_0 is omitted. Degree constraints force the purported cycle to split into the two 5-cycles a_1-a_0-a_4-b_4-b_1-a_1 and a_2-a_3-b_3-b_0-b_2-a_2, rather than forming one Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary: The Petersen graph explicitly satisfies every hypothesis but is non-Hamiltonian, so the statement is false.
